best: Found that wrapping the clients routed nothing on its own and fixed the three real blockers — seed=0 on every OpenAI call, the pinned gpt-4o-2024-05-13 reviewer, and a claude-3-5-sonnet id that isn't a catalog model — each as a separate revertable commit, with live 200s confirming gpt-4o on /v1/responses and claude-sonnet-4-6 on /v1/messages.

Measured the LiteLLM boundary instead of assuming it: install_litellm() carries aider's OpenAI turns to Router while LiteLLM's Anthropic handler builds its own client and goes straight to api.anthropic.com — and said plainly that this is probably the largest share of a default run's spend and is still vendor traffic.

Built the ensemble-without-n branch (the only way the app's biggest step can route at all), kept the samples independent, quantified the up-to-5x input-cost consequence honestly, and contradicted its own tooling where `check --all` optimistically reported DeepSeek/Gemini sites as routing when the trace showed them kept on the vendor host.
misses: aider's Claude turns — the dominant cost of a default run, by the report's own reasoning — were left entirely on the vendor and downgraded to a proposal, when a low-risk mechanism (point LiteLLM's Anthropic path at Router via api_base/base-URL config with a catalog id, behind the same disable flag, on a branch) was buildable and testable here; the biggest unmigrated spend is described rather than moved.

The broken Claude branch it discovered (temperature TypeError on the installed SDK) was left untouched, so the default --model path is never exercised end-to-end through Router — m5's 'routes today' rests on a hand-constructed messages.create call, not on the app's own code path. An expert would have at least put the one-line fix on a branch so the claim could be verified through get_response_from_llm.

Flex tier and model fallbacks — the two highest-leverage Router-only levers for a long-running unattended pipeline with no human waiting — were only gestured at (and are missing from the item list as delivered), and no concurrency plan accompanies i2, which turns the biggest step into 5 sequential full-paper reviews and multiplies the ICLR benchmark's 500x5 wall-clock.
wrong: m5's rationale is self-contradictory with n1: it pays $3/$15 for claude-sonnet-4-6 instead of $2/$10 for claude-sonnet-5 specifically to keep temperature, while n1 reports the installed anthropic SDK cannot accept temperature at all — if n1 is right, the cheaper map was the correct choice and the stated reason evaporates.

'Nothing was proposed for structured output: this app uses none' is wrong about the code. The app's entire LLM protocol is JSON-in-markdown parsed by extract_json_between_markers, with reflection loops that exist partly to recover from malformed output — a JSON-schema/structured-output proposal is a direct, grounded robustness win and was skipped.

The report's route truth diverges from the outside check on four sites (llm.py:84, :236, :251, :264 are validated as verified routes; the report lists them as staying with the vendor) and the reviewer is left to adjudicate. The reason given (host not unlocked, untranslatable n) is plausible, but a bare contradiction on coverage is the one thing a reviewer cannot resolve from the dashboard.

i1's headline savings ('about half' for gpt-4o-mini, 'about 90%' for cached Claude reads) are transplanted from measurements elsewhere plus catalog cache_read prices, with no A/B on this app's prompts — disclosed, but they are the sole justification for the improvement, and the 1,024-token minimum means the short idea-reflection prompts may see nothing.

The vendored runtime and the compiled router_policy.py were produced by hand (the outside check raises its own runtime-edit flag), so the actual request path differs from a tool-generated one and is not independently reproducible — a real risk left standing rather than resolved.

As delivered, the report is truncated mid-i4, and two improvements the 'reviewed' section promises (fallback candidates, a move to Flex-eligible models) have no items at all, so a third of the claimed improvement set is unreviewable.
